chunks: And it is narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq:

He wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that Durrah bint Muqātil had died and left an estate consisting of shares in such-and-such a place. She had bequeathed to our master, from her shares, more than one-third, and we are her executors. We wished to convey that to our master, so if he commands us to carry out the bequest in the manner it stands, we will carry it out; and if he commands us otherwise, we will comply with his command in all that he commands us, if Allah, Most High, wills.

So he عليه السلام wrote in his own handwriting: "No more than one-third is binding for her in her estate. But if you show generosity, and you are the heirs, then it is permissible for you, if Allah wills."

key_terms.أَشْقَاصًا: undivided shares or portions in property
key_terms.الثُّلُثُ: one-third of the estate, the binding limit of a bequest

ai.seo_question: Can a bequest exceed one-third of a deceased person's estate in Shia law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on bequests, stating that a deceased person may only bind one-third of the estate through a will. Any amount beyond one-third depends on the heirs' consent, and if they voluntarily allow it, that is permissible.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5429 - It is narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Ishaq that he wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (as), informing him:

"Durrah bint Muqatil has passed away and left behind an estate consisting of portions in a certain place. She bequeathed more than one-third of her estate to our master, and we are her executors. We wished to inform our master about this matter. If you command us to carry out the will as it is, we will do so. But if you command otherwise, we will adhere to your instruction in all that you command us, God willing."

So Abu Al-Hasan (as) replied in his own handwriting:
"She is entitled to only one-third of her estate. However, if you, as the heirs, choose to be generous, it is permissible for you, God willing."
